title: Geometric stalks commute with pro-etale inverse image
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and use the small pro-etale sites and compatible universes and small skeletons of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], with $\Omega$ in the chosen bound, and put $\bar y=f\circ\bar x$. For a sheaf $F$ of sets or of abelian groups on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $f^{-1}F$ be the inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Stalks mean the colimits over pointed weakly etale neighbourhoods of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
 c_{f,\bar x,F}:(f^{-1}F)_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar y},
$$
natural in $F$; for abelian sheaves it is additive. Explicitly, for every morphism $h:F\to G$,
$$
 c_{f,\bar x,G}\circ(f^{-1}h)_{\bar x}=h_{\bar y}\circ c_{f,\bar x,F}.
$$
In particular, equality of the inverse images of two sheaf maps implies equality of their stalk maps at every geometric point of $Y$ obtained by composing $f$ with a geometric point of $X$. No finiteness, separation, smoothness or surjectivity assumption on $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the pro-etale site point attached to the geometric point x. Its fibre assigns to each neighbourhood the arrows from x to that neighbourhood, lifted to the larger universe. The point axioms use finite-limit preservation and the fact that every pro-etale covering lifts the algebraically closed field point; the latter is the existing weakly-etale section theorem, applied after the fpqc/base-change description of the pro-etale topology.

The category of elements of this point is equivalent to the pointed pro-etale neighbourhood category. The resulting final-colimit isomorphism identifies the point sheaf fibre with the geometric stalk, and its germ equation identifies each colimit coprojection with evaluation at the corresponding pointed neighbourhood.

The pullback adjunction on over-categories identifies maps from x to the base change of V with maps from x followed by f to V. This natural bijection is inverseImagePointFiberIso, implemented by Adjunction.compCoyonedaIso (Over.mapPullbackAdj f). On the specified lifted neighbourhood it sends z to its first projection, which is N.hom by the hypothesis of the germ clause. Hence the comapped point is isomorphic to the point of x followed by f. Base change preserves finite limits and covers by the declarations in the inverse-image module. All categories of elements are initially small in universe u+1; equivalences transport the needed colimits.

Apply the general site-point inverse-image comparison and its proved unit-germ formula to proEtaleBaseChange f. The comparison is the composite of the stalk identification, the generic sheaf-fibre comparison, the point isomorphism induced by the fibre equivalence, and the inverse stalk identification. The germ equation follows from the upstream unit-germ lemma; naturality is the naturality of the composite isomorphism, and equality reflection follows by cancellation.

Specialize the generic construction first to Type (u+1), where the required products and sheafification exist, and then to AddCommGrpCat. The latter specialization is an isomorphism in the coefficient category, hence additive, and both satisfy the displayed naturality and reflection clauses.
